post.summary: Assign a B2B entity to a user
post.description:
Sets assignedToId on a B2BLead, B2BClient or B2BDeal and writes an AssignmentLog row when the assignee actually changes.

**Notes:** Wrapped in withAuditLog (entity ORDER, action ASSIGN). Instantiates its own PrismaClient and disconnects per request. For B2BLead it also stamps assignedAt.

_Source: `app/api/assign/route.ts`_

_Auth: `other: reads getServerSession(authOptions) only to resolve the acting admin; falls back to admin id 1 and never rejects unauthenticated callers`_

Creates VendorPincodes rows linking a vendor to each supplied pincode entry.

**Notes:** No auth, no validation and no existence checks. Errors are swallowed and returned with HTTP 200 and success:false, so callers must inspect the body. Imports BACKEND_API from env but does not use it.

_Source: `app/api/assignpincodestovendor/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

200.description: Failure is also returned with HTTP 200

post.summary: Assign a lead to a vendor
post.description:
Validates lead availability, vendor status, lead capacity and credit balance, then locks the lead (and eligible sibling leads of the same customer) to the vendor, charging the vendor's credits.

**Notes:** SIDE EFFECTS: deducts vendor credits (dynamic credit points from the pricing system), may lock additional leads of the same customer up to the vendor's remaining capacity, sends vendor email via sendEmailNotification and a Firebase push via firebaseMessaging, writes an admin activity log and invalidates the Redis orders cache. Error codes: INVALID_JSON, VALIDATION_ERROR, LEAD_NOT_FOUND, CUSTOMER_DELETED, VENDOR_NOT_FOUND, VENDOR_INACTIVE, MAX_LEADS_REACHED, ASSIGNMENT_FAILED, DATABASE_ERROR, INTERNAL_ERROR.

_Source: `app/api/assignvendor/route.ts`_

_Auth: `other: no enforcement — getServerSession is consulted only to attribute the admin activity log`_

get.summary: Get today's live attendance map data

**Notes:** Takes no parameters; the date is fixed to today at 00:00 UTC.

_Source: `app/api/attendance/live-map/route.ts`_

post.summary: Bulk import onboarding leads from CSV
post.description:
Parses an uploaded CSV of vendor leads (business name, phone, address, optional city and device type), normalises phone numbers, skips duplicates and existing vendors, and bulk-inserts the rest.

**Notes:** multipart/form-data — do not set Content-Type manually. Wrapped in withAuditLog, which writes an AdminActivityLog row when a NextAuth session cookie is present but does NOT itdoes not enforce auth itself. Since 2026-09-05 middleware.ts is deny-by-default for /api/*, so an admin session is required at the edge. Only the first 10 row errors are returned; totalErrors carries the full count.

_Source: `app/api/onboarding-b2c/upload/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

post.summary: Reassign an order to another vendor
post.description:
Runs the shared lead-lock reassignment routine to move an order to a different vendor. A non-empty reason is mandatory because the order is being taken away from the current vendor. Invalidates the orders cache on both success and failure.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. Shares processLeadLock with /api/assignvendor; mutates vendor assignment and credit locks. Note the lowercase leadid/vendorid field names.

_Source: `app/api/reassignvendor/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

example.message: A reason is required to reassign an order away from a vendor

ErrorEnvelope.description: Plain error envelope `{ error }` used by most routes. `error` is a human-readable message.

pincodes.description: One entry per VendorPincodes row to create; each becomes the row's `pincode` value (the column is an int array).

vendorid.description: Vendor id to attach the coverage to.

reason.description: Reason for taking the order away; blank or missing 400s

action.description: Optional action passed through to processLeadLock

file.description: CSV file; header must contain business/name/shop, phone/mobile/contact and address/location columns

source.description: Lead source label; defaults to 'Manual Upload'

city.description: City override for every row; 'none' means unset

deviceType.description: Device type override for every row; 'none' means unset

entityId.description: Id of the entity to reassign.

toUserId.description: New assignee id; null clears the assignment (and skips the log).

fromUserId.description: Previous assignee, recorded on the AssignmentLog.

reason.description: Free-text reason stored on the log.

vendorid.description: Vendor id (note the all-lowercase key expected by the upstream)

leadid.description: MasterLeads leadId to assign. Must be non-empty and currently unassigned.

vendorid.description: Vendors vendorId to assign it to. Vendor must have status 'live'.

reason.description: Reason recorded with the credit deduction / assignment.

action.description: Optional action tag forwarded to the lead-lock routine.

status.description: AttendanceStatus enum value, e.g. PRESENT | LATE | ON_FIELD | CHECKED_OUT | DISPUTED | ABSENT.

remarks.description: Reason for the override; appended to existing remarks.

nextFollowUp.description: ISO date for the next follow-up, or null to clear

assignedTo.description: Admin id to assign the lead to

createdBy.description: Admin recorded on the generated log rows

SuccessMessageEnvelope.description: Envelope `{ success, message }`; `success` is `true` on 2xx and `false` on error responses.

cookieAuth.name: next-auth.session-token
cookieAuth.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie from logging in to the admin panel. On HTTPS the cookie name is `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

cronBearer.description: `LINODE_CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token — every cron job goes through `assertCronAuth` in `lib/linode/cron-auth.ts`, which reads only this variable (despite some jobs being non-Linode).

unverifiedAccessToken.name: Authorization
unverifiedAccessToken.description: Legacy customer routes: an `accessToken` cookie or an `Authorization` header must be PRESENT, but the value is never verified. Not real authentication.

adsWebhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
adsWebhookSecret.description: `ADS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, sent either as the `x-webhook-secret` header or as a `secret` field in the JSON body. If the env var is unset the route rejects every call with 401 (it does not fall through to unauthenticated access).

webhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
webhookSecret.description: Generic `x-webhook-secret` header check for an inbound webhook.

cronSecretBearer.description: `CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token, compared with `bearerMatches` in `lib/auth/secret-compare.ts`. Distinct from `cronBearer`, which uses `LINODE_CRON_SECRET`.
